title: A complete Noetherian local domain has a nonempty regular open
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Assume that $R$ is a domain (a nonzero ring without zero divisors) and is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Then there exists a nonempty Zariski-open subset $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] such that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every $\mathfrak p\in U$.

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, with J-0 expanded by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: Write $A=R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-domain-finite-over-regular], choose a complete regular local subring $A_0\subseteq A$ such that $A$ is a finite $A_0$-module. It is a domain because it is a subring of the domain $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], every prime localization of $A_0$ is regular local. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ itself is a nonempty regular open: it contains the prime $(0)$. Put $K_0=\operatorname{Frac}(A_0)$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. The extension $K/K_0$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree].

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, proof; J-0 means a nonempty regular open by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: We will use concrete models for all intermediate fields $K_0\subseteq M\subseteq K$: set $B(M)=A\cap M$, an $A_0$-submodule and subring of $A$. It is finite over $A_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], and hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. Every finite module generating family also generates the algebra, so $A_0\to B(M)$ is of finite type. The next step verifies that its fraction field is exactly $M$.

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, proof; J-0 means a nonempty regular open by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], every $a\in A$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A_0$. For $a
e0$, cancel powers of $a$ from a relation with zero constant term (the ambient ring is a domain), obtaining $a^m+c_{m-1}a^{m-1}+\cdots+c_0=0$ with $c_0
e0$. Thus $a^{-1}=-(a^{m-1}+c_{m-1}a^{m-2}+\cdots+c_1)/c_0$ belongs to $(A_0\setminus\{0\})^{-1}A$. This proves that this localization equals $K$. Every $x\in M$ therefore has the form $a/s$ with $a\in A$ and $0
e s\in A_0$; then $a=sx\in A\cap M=B(M)$. Hence $\operatorname{Frac}(B(M))=M$, and every $x\in M$ admits a nonzero $s\in A_0$ with $sx\in B(M)$.

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, proof; J-0 means a nonempty regular open by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] to $K/K_0$. Let $M_0$ be the separable algebraic closure of $K_0$ inside $K$. Then $M_0/K_0$ is separable and $K/M_0$ is purely inseparable; all these extensions are finite since $K/K_0$ is finite. The injection $A_0\to B(M_0)$ has finite type by step 2 and fraction-field extension $M_0/K_0$ by step 3. Applying [lem-exc-j0-separable-finite-type-ascent] to the regular open of $A_0$ from step 1 gives a nonempty regular open in $\operatorname{Spec}B(M_0)$. If $M_0=K$, then $B(M_0)=A$ and this is the conclusion. This includes characteristic zero.

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, proof; J-0 means a nonempty regular open by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: Otherwise the characteristic is a prime $p>0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower], choose a finite tower $M_0\subset M_1\subset\cdots\subset M_n=K$, where $M_i=M_{i-1}(\alpha_i)$, $[M_i:M_{i-1}]=p$, and $\alpha_i^p\in M_{i-1}$ is not a $p$th power there. Set $B_i=B(M_i)$. We induct on $i$ on the assertion that $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ contains a nonempty regular open. Step 4 is the base $i=0$. Fix $1\le i\le n$ and assume the assertion for $B=B_{i-1}$; write $E=B_i$ and $M=M_{i-1}$.

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, proof; J-0 means a nonempty regular open by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne s\in A_0$ with $z=s\alpha_i\in E$ by step 3. Then $M_i=M(z)$ and $b=z^p=s^p\alpha_i^p$ lies in $A\cap M=B$. It is not a $p$th power in $M$, since division by $s^p$ would make $\alpha_i^p$ one. For $C=B[z]\subseteq E$, the map $B[T]/(T^p-b)\to C$, $T\mapsto z$, is an isomorphism: division by the monic polynomial reduces every element to degree less than $p$, and a nonzero relation of that degree would contradict $[M(z):M]=p$. In particular $\operatorname{Frac}(C)=M_i=\operatorname{Frac}(E)$.

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, proof; J-0 means a nonempty regular open by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text:
The ring $B$ is a domain of characteristic $p$ and of finite type over the Noetherian complete local ring $A_0$ (steps 1 and 2). Since $b$ is not a $p$th power in $M=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-nonzero-on-non-pth-power] gives an additive derivation $D:B	o B$ with $D(b)
e0$. Choose $0
e h\in B$ with $D(h)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$ contained in the nonempty regular open supplied by the induction hypothesis; here $D(h)$ denotes the principal open, not the value of the derivation. Such a choice is possible because principal opens form the basis of the Zariski topology. Set $g=hD(b)
e0$ and $S=B_g$.

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, proof; J-0 means a nonempty regular open by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: The ring $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Its prime local rings are $B_{\mathfrak q}$ for $g\notin\mathfrak q$, hence regular local by the choice of $h$; explicitly the two iterated fraction maps send $(a/g^r)/u$ to $a/(g^r u)$ and are inverse. Thus $S$ is a regular ring by the definition [def-weil-regular-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends], $D$ extends to a derivation on $S$; its value on $b$ is the image of $D(b)$, a unit since $g=hD(b)$ is inverted. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-degree-p-extension-regular], with $n=p$, gives that $S[T]/(T^p-b)$ is regular. The presentation in step 6 identifies this ring with $C_g$ by localizing the coefficients and the generator $T\mapsto z$.

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, proof; J-0 means a nonempty regular open by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: To pass from $C$ to $E$, take finite $A_0$-module generators $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $E$ from step 2. Since $\operatorname{Frac}(C)=\operatorname{Frac}(E)$, write $e_j=u_j/v_j$ with $u_j,v_j\in C$ and $v_j\ne0$. Set $c=\prod_jv_j\ne0$ (the empty product is $1$). Every $e_j$ belongs to $C_c$, so their $A_0$-span $E$ lies in $C_c$; the reverse inclusion after localization follows from $C\subseteq E$. Thus $E_c=C_c$ and $E_{gc}=C_{gc}$. This explicitly supplies the shrinking needed before applying the regularity statement about $C$ to $E$.

source.place: Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0, proof; J-0 means a nonempty regular open by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring], localizing the regular ring $C_g$ further at $c$ gives a regular ring $C_{gc}=E_{gc}$. The principal open $D_E(gc)$ is nonempty since $E$ is a domain and $gc\ne0$: it contains $(0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] it is the image of $\operatorname{Spec}E_{gc}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}E$. For a prime $\mathfrak q$ in that open, its local ring is $E_{\mathfrak q}$ by the same fraction maps as in step 8, and is regular local since $E_{gc}$ is regular. This completes the induction. At $i=n$ we have $B_n=A\cap K=A$, so the resulting principal open is the required $U$.

Proof steps: (1) 032D gives a regular complete subring A_0, all of Spec A_0 is a regular open, and the fraction-field extension K/K_0 is finite. (2-3) The models B(M) = A ∩ M are finite over A_0 and have fraction field M, by the integral-equation inverse formula. (4) The separable part M_0 is handled by 07PB, with every hypothesis checked; finite separable algebraic meets the 030O definition with an empty transcendence basis. (5) The 09HI p-th-root tower gives an explicit induction with its base and claim stated. (6) z = sα_i makes B[T]/(T^p - b) ≅ C (the map is injective by the degree-p argument), and b is not a p-th power. (7-8) 07PH gives D, the principal open D(h) is chosen, the derivation is extended to B_g by 07PE(2), and 07PG with n = p makes C_g regular. (9) A common denominator c gives E_c = C_c. (10) The localization is regular and D_E(gc) is a nonempty regular open. The induction ends at B_n = A. Each step is correct and uses only what the cited statements say. There are no new nodes and no duplicates: only the item and its parent mention 07PI. The 8 tool uses are generic algebra used as black boxes and are accepted; no SGA source is cited.
